title: Leaf outlines, species
question: Can a leaf's species be read from its outline?

source.name: Outlines of Swedish leaves (figshare 14551005), from the Swedish Leaf dataset
source.citation: Leroi, Marsland & Salili-James, Outlines of Swedish leaves, figshare DOI 10.6084/m9.figshare.14551005 (CC BY 4.0, https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/); outlines extracted by those authors from the photographs of Söderkvist, O. J. O. (2001) Swedish Leaf dataset, MSc thesis, Linköping University (page states no terms; a Zenodo record listing Söderkvist as creator, 19663514, is CC BY 4.0, uploader not identified); modified here: resampled by arc length, see data/leaves_outlines.ATTRIBUTION.md

correspondence: arc length from the source's start point (kept: it is a landmark)
preprocessing: outline resampled by arc length from 150 to 100 points

closed outlines keep the source's start point: 69% of them already start within 10% of the perimeter of their best cyclic shift to the Fréchet mean, so the start is a landmark (re-rooting would only blur it)

landmarks_lr.accuracy_sd_def: sd of fold_accuracies over the folds, ddof=0 (population sd)
landmarks_lr.cm_layout: rows true, cols predicted, class order
landmarks_lr.note: mean and tangent PCA fitted on all shapes (label-free); scaler and regression refit in every fold
landmarks_lr.worst_note: p / p_cv: out-of-fold probabilities; p_engine: the engine (fitted on all shapes) on the same shape

engine.decision: p = softmax(lr_coef @ x + lr_intercept), x = (scores - scaler_mean) / scaler_scale
engine.correspondence: arc length from the source's start point (kept: it is a landmark)

spline_lr.accuracy_sd_def: sd of fold_accuracies over the folds, ddof=0 (population sd)
spline_lr.cm_layout: rows true, cols predicted, class order
spline_lr.note: mean and tangent PCA fitted on all shapes (label-free); scaler and regression refit in every fold
spline_lr.worst_note: p / p_cv: out-of-fold probabilities; p_engine: the engine (fitted on all shapes) on the same shape

engine.decision: p = softmax(lr_coef @ x + lr_intercept), x = (scores - scaler_mean) / scaler_scale
engine.correspondence: arc length from the source's start point (kept: it is a landmark)

spline_lr.spline: BSplineCurve(M=12, closed=True).fit(points): least-squares control points with arc-length parameters; the engine classifies the (M, 2) control polygon

size_lr.accuracy_sd_def: sd of fold_accuracies over the folds, ddof=0 (population sd)
size_lr.cm_layout: rows true, cols predicted, class order
size_lr.feature: log centroid size (Frobenius norm of the centred points, in the data's units)
size_lr.note: baseline: size is the only input; never a headline number (excluded from best_accuracy)

pointnet_probe.accuracy_measure: linear probe fitted on the fit embeddings, scored on the untouched 25 % hold-out
pointnet_probe.accuracy_select_measure: the same probe scored on the 20 % select slice: the number that chose the epoch
pointnet_probe.accuracy_sd_def: sd of fold_accuracies of the 5-fold probe inside the hold-out, ddof=0; not an uncertainty of `accuracy`
pointnet_probe.protocol: stratified 75/25 hold-out, seed 0; epoch chosen on a 20 % slice of the training part
pointnet_probe.cv: 5-fold StratifiedKFold(shuffle, random_state=0) linear probe on the validation embeddings (as the tutorial did)
pointnet_probe.split: train_test_split(test_size=0.25, stratify=labels, random_state=0); the training part split again with test_size=0.2 (stratified, random_state=0) into fit / select
pointnet_probe.training: SupConLoss(temperature 0.07), Adam lr 0.0003, weight decay 0.001, batch 64, random rotation + jitter augmentation, best epoch by the probe on the select slice
pointnet_probe.preprocessing: centre each cloud, divide it by its own RMS radius (unit size per cloud: size removed), then by input_scale (1 by construction)
pointnet_probe.cm_layout: rows true, cols predicted, class order; validation split only
pointnet_probe.worst_note: p / p_engine: the hold-out probe's probabilities (one fit, no cross-validation)

onnx_info.input: points (batch, n_points, 2) float32, centred, divided by the cloud's own RMS radius, then divided by input_scale

cyclic_shift_alignment.criterion: applied unless at least 50% of the outlines already start within 10% of the perimeter of their best shift

engine.decision: p = softmax(lr_coef @ x + lr_intercept), x = (scores - scaler_mean) / scaler_scale
engine.correspondence: arc length from the source's start point (kept: it is a landmark)

timing.note: wall-clock seconds; not deterministic and not part of the results
